transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-05-22 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~47m
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Maya Rodriguez (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood CSM); Ben Park (CoralWave Platform Lead), Priya Shah (CoralWave Security), Liam O'Neill (CoralWave ML Infra), Sofia Ruiz (CoralWave Product)

[00:00] Alex Kim: hey everyone thanks for joining, um, we'll try to keep this tight, go over access, staging issues, and next steps for the benchmark. Maya and Jordan on deck.
[00:18] Ben Park: yeah thanks Alex, on our side we've got Priya and Liam — just to reiterate our goal: get a staging gateway running with KMS-backed keys and SSO before we run the larger throughput tests.
[00:30] Maya Rodriguez: cool, quick status from Redwood: we pushed the gateway image to your staging repo yesterday, the init script needs the SAML metadata and the Kms policy. small note — sometimes the K V cache flag is mis-placed in the template, so watch for that.
[00:50] Priya Shah: right, that's where we hit snags last night — the init failed with a permissions error when requesting the customer-managed key. Liam dug in but we wanted to clarify the exact IAM role mapping.
[01:05] Liam O'Neill: yeah, the error looked like 403 from KMS, we suspect the service account wasn't allowed to decrypt the test key. I can paste the logs after.
[01:16] Alex Kim: ok that's expected, we'll share a minimal IAM policy snippet. Maya — can you confirm the exact role name Redwood expects?
[01:24] Maya Rodriguez: sure it's redwood-poc-ingress-role, but, uhh, in the current chart it's redwood-poc-ingress-role-prod, so that mismatch is probably the culprit. we'll send corrected helm values.
[01:40] Ben Park: good catch. separate thing — our SSO team says they can produce the SAML metadata but need a list of callback URLs.
[01:48] Jordan Lee: callback URLs are in the onboarding doc but to be safe: https://staging.coralwave.internal/auth/callback and the gateway health endpoint — we'll include both in the doc.
[02:02] Sofia Ruiz: small product question — when you say KV cache, does that mean we persist user session state across calls? there was concern about PII.
[02:12] Maya Rodriguez: brief answer: KV cache is only model KV cache — it's model-specific key-value cache to speed up autoregressive decoding; it doesn't store user PII. we'll flag exact retention windows in the security pack though.
[02:30] Priya Shah: please do, because our compliance team wants retention windows and encryption at rest details.
[02:36] Alex Kim: understood. Maya will attach the security-compliance-pack; it includes SOC2 checklist, KMS integration steps, and data flow diagram.
[02:46] Liam O'Neill: switching to perf — we ran a short smoke run on hosted RedWood API yesterday, average p50 was ~95ms but we saw p95 spikes to ~260ms. want to understand if that's networking or model cold start.
[03:05] Maya Rodriguez: spike sounds like cold-starts and occasional batching latency. in staging we recommend enabling prefix caching and setting min-batch-size to 2 to reduce tail latency. also quant profile can help if you're ok with small quality tradeoff.
[03:22] Ben Park: what's the suggested quant profile? we've tried 4-bit on local tests and saw hallucination increase.
[03:30] Maya Rodriguez: for production we'd recommend dynamic-8q or 6-bit for LLMs similar to your model; 4-bit is aggressive unless you retrain/finetune. we can run a side-by-side quality eval as part of the benchmark.
[03:46] Alex Kim: note — we can also fall back to hosted variants if the private gateway hits perf issues; Redwood Dedicated variant could be an option for predictable throughput.
[03:58] Priya Shah: one more security ask — do you support HSM-backed KMS or only cloud KMS?
[04:06] Maya Rodriguez: Redwood supports cloud KMS with customer-managed keys; HSM integration is available for Dedicated/Private with additional onboarding — we'll flag that in the security pack.
[04:18] Ben Park: great. about the gateway routing error — Liam, you had a trace?
[04:24] Liam O'Neill: yes, we saw 502s between gateway and the inference-worker on brief intervals. stack trace points to a TLS negotiation timeout; suspect egress rules or proxy.
[04:36] Jordan Lee: can you confirm egress IP ranges? we sent a list but maybe staging uses NAT at different range — we'll reconcile.
[04:45] Ben Park: we'll double-check and open a ticket if needed.
[04:50] Alex Kim: ok for next week's gated benchmark, suggested test plan: 10k short prompts (<=64 tokens), prefix caching on/off, KV cache enabled, SSO+KMS exercised, and record p50/p95, error rate. sound good?
[05:06] Ben Park: yes — also include a throughput ramp to 150 req/min to validate autoscaling.
[05:12] Maya Rodriguez: we'll add that. also we'll include token-level cost estimate so you can compare Dedicated vs hosted.
[05:20] Sofia Ruiz: quick question on audit logs — can we get per-request audit with request IDs and auth subject?
[05:27] Maya Rodriguez: yes, Redwood Console exposes per-request tracing and you can pull logs to your SIEM via our log-forwarder; we'll include the exporter config.
[05:40] Priya Shah: thanks. can you clarify retention defaults for those logs?
[05:45] Maya Rodriguez: default is 30 days for the pilot; enterprise retention add-on is available. we'll include retention options in the doc.
[05:56] Ben Park: switching to timeline — we want to run the gated benchmark by next Thursday to decide on Dedicated in early June. is that feasible?
[06:06] Alex Kim: yes, feasible if SSO metadata and key access are resolved this week.
[06:12] Liam O'Neill: I'll attach the staging logs and the TLS trace to the ticket after this call.
[06:18] Jordan Lee: perfect. we'll also schedule a 60m smoke test to validate gateway routing — propose Tue 2025-05-27 14:00 UTC.
[06:28] Ben Park: that works for our infra team.
[06:32] Sofia Ruiz: one more product nuance — latency SLOs we discussed: is p50 < 120ms and p95 < 300ms — are those realistic on your hosted flows?
[06:42] Maya Rodriguez: for short prompts that's realistic on hosted; for private with current config you'd need KV cache and some batching — otherwise p95 can spike. we'll run benchmarks to confirm.
[06:52] Priya Shah: anything else on compliance?
[06:56] Alex Kim: we'll share the security pack and an anonymized audit log sample.
[07:02] Ben Park: ok great.
[07:05] Maya Rodriguez: small note — in the helm values we saw an env var spelled REDW00D_GATEWAY in one stub, might be a copy-paste; watch for that.
[07:15] (laughter) Alex Kim: uh-oh, devops humor.
[07:20] Ben Park: we'll grep for that.
[07:24] Jordan Lee: final recap — Redwood shares security docs and IAM snippet (Maya), Alex kicks off benchmark with the test corpus once we confirm SSO (Alex), CoralWave provides SAML metadata and opens support ticket for gateway TLS (Ben/Liam), Jordan books smoke test for Tue 25th.
[07:44] Sofia Ruiz: minor ask — can we get a cost delta estimate between hosted vs dedicated per 1M tokens?
[07:50] Maya Rodriguez: yes, we'll include a spreadsheet with model profiles and token unit pricing.
[08:00] Alex Kim: cool, thanks everyone. any blockers we didn't cover?
[08:04] Priya Shah: none from security beyond KMS role.
[08:08] Ben Park: all good. thanks.
[08:11] Alex Kim: thanks, we'll follow up in the shared drive and put the action items in CRM.

[End of transcript]
notes: Call included AE+SE+CSM from Redwood; customer prioritized SSO/KMS and a gateway smoke test. Minor transcription artifacts present (product names and env var names).
